quarterly.period_note: Year-end (31 December 2020) position from Southeast Bank's own audited annual report multi-year "Key Financial Data and Ratios" summary table. CONSOLIDATED (Group) basis. Southeast Bank prepares its multi-year "Key Financial Data and Ratios" summary tables on the consolidated basis, so no Solo/Standalone multi-year series exists in these reports; this was verified against the underlying statements (FY2025 total assets 554,424.56m consolidated vs 551,643.08m solo, a 0.50% difference; FY2014 236,608.40m consolidated vs 236,216.15m solo, 0.17%). The bank's subsidiaries (Southeast Bank Capital Services, SBL Exchange entities) are small relative to the bank, so the consolidated series tracks the solo series closely, but the basis differs from the Solo-basis series used for banks elsewhere in this dataset. Total liabilities are calculated as total assets minus total shareholders' equity (the source tables do not print a total-liabilities line). Net interest income is calculated as Interest Income minus Interest Expenses. Provision for Loans is calculated as Provision for Unclassified Loans plus Provision for Classified Loans. Total Expenditure is Interest Expenses plus Operating (Non-Interest) Expenses throughout. The composition of Total Income changes with the table format: for FY2011-FY2019 Investment Income is a separate line that sits alongside Non-Interest Income, so Total Income = Interest Income + Investment Income + Non-Interest Income (verified: FY2014 19,233.89 + 5,274.27 + 3,158.93 = 27,667.09 = reported Total Income; FY2019 26,258.88 + 5,288.98 + 4,844.75 = 36,392.61 = reported Total Income). From FY2020 the tables fold Investment Income into Non-Interest Income, so Total Income = Interest Income + Non-Interest Income (verified: FY2023 22,047.89 + 14,118.37 = 36,166.26 = reported Total Income). Investment Income is still reported separately in both formats and is retained as its own line item here, so for FY2020 onwards it must not be added to Non-Interest Income when reconstructing Total Income. Southeast Bank's FY2020 report is in this archive, but its detailed "Key Financial Data and Ratios" table extracts as mojibake (the PDF embeds a subsetted font whose encoding pdftotext cannot map), so the detailed line items are taken from the FY2021 report -- the earliest report carrying FY2020 whose table extracts cleanly. Both of the FY2020 report's readable tables were used to validate it: its "Last 10 Years' Financial Indicators" table (p.42) confirms every headline figure, and the numeric column of the garbled table confirms Provision for Unclassified Loans at 3,301.06. That last point matters: the FY2021 report prints 3,636.01 for that line, which is contradicted by the FY2020 report itself and by the FY2022, FY2023 and FY2024 reports, so 3,301.06 is used. Return on Equity is recorded as 7.14%, the figure in the FY2020 report's own ten-year table; the FY2021 report and every later one restate it as 6.91%. Reserve fund is calculated as equity minus paid-up capital (29,703.77 - 11,889.41); the source row (28,483.13) reproduces Total Capital (40,372.53), not equity.

insights.methodology: Derived from bank_financials/SOUTHEASTB/quarterly/*.json (FY2011-FY2025 year-end, consolidated basis) and ratios_timeseries.json. Every figure quoted below is a reported value from Southeast Bank's own audited annual-report summary tables, or an explicitly-labelled ratio computed from them (provision coverage = provision for classified loans / classified loans; net interest margin proxy = net interest income / period-end interest-earning assets; price-to-book = year-end DSE price / NAV per share; capital surplus % = reported surplus / derived required capital). NPL%, ROA%, ROE%, CRAR%, cost-to-income and LDR are the bank's own reported ratios, not recomputed — the bank computes ROA/ROE on average balances, so period-end recomputations are stored separately in ratios_timeseries.json and differ. No figure is interpolated or estimated.

risk_signals.statement: Classified loans rose for four consecutive years at 40-62% a year, from 9,939.76m (FY2020) to 54,813.65m (FY2024) — a 451% increase — taking the reported NPL ratio from 3.10% to 14.82%. The annual increments were +61.33% (FY2021), +40.75% (FY2022), +50.20% (FY2023) and +61.69% (FY2024). Over the same four years gross loans grew only 15.7% (322,251.46m to 372,907.25m), so the NPL build-up is deterioration in the existing book, not dilution by fast growth.

The FY2025 headline improvement — NPL down from 14.82% to 7.51%, classified loans down 48.69% from 54,813.65m to 28,127.54m — is not corroborated by the provision movement. Provision for classified loans fell 63.1% (30,029.27m to 11,072.11m) while provision for unclassified loans rose 332.8% (2,680.38m to 11,601.19m), which is the signature of exposures being reclassified out of the NPL bucket rather than recovered in cash. Specific provision coverage of NPLs consequently fell from 54.78% to 39.36%, its lowest reading in the entire 15-year series except FY2015 (32.30%). Total loan-loss provisions fell 10,036.35m year on year (32,709.65m to 22,673.30m), and that release is comparable in size to the entire 2,620.96m improvement in profit before tax (1,873.72m to 4,494.68m).

Southeast Bank has fallen below its Basel minimum capital requirement in three separate years of the series: FY2017 (deficit 1,285.07m, CRAR 10.84%, 3.67% short of requirement), FY2019 (deficit 3,071.28m, CRAR 11.52%, 7.84% short) and FY2024 (deficit 3,062.82m, CRAR 11.64%, 6.86% short). The Tier-1 ratio has never exceeded 9.14% (FY2011) in the whole series and bottomed at 6.79% in FY2017; even after the FY2025 recovery to 13.61% CRAR the Tier-1 ratio is only 9.13%, meaning the capital position leans heavily on Tier-2 instruments (16,819.70m of a 51,096.18m total).

Net interest income as a share of interest-earning assets has fallen almost without interruption from 1.66% (FY2016) to 0.43% (FY2025), a 74% erosion. In FY2025 the bank earned 33,295.91m of interest income against 31,180.36m of interest expense — a net interest income of just 2,115.55m on 496,349.88m of earning assets. The bank's own reported spread confirms the squeeze: 5.20% (FY2014) to 1.84% (FY2025). Earnings are now carried by non-interest income (17,702.47m in FY2025, 8.4x the net interest income), which is a materially less stable base.

Return on equity fell from 16.51% (FY2014) to a series low of 1.36% (FY2024), and averaged 6.15% across FY2017-FY2024 — eight consecutive years of single-digit returns. Return on assets fell from 1.67% (FY2014) to 0.09% (FY2024). FY2024 net profit was 432.64m against 3,836.94m in FY2014, an 88.7% decline in nominal terms while total assets grew 131% over the same span. The FY2025 recovery to 10.16% ROE and 0.61% ROA is the best result since FY2015, but it rests on the provision release described above.

FY2024 net profit after tax was 432.64m, down 79.7% from 2,133.83m in FY2023 and equivalent to EPS of 0.32 against 1.66 a year earlier. Operating profit actually rose that year, from 8,857.63m to 11,721.29m, so the collapse happened entirely below the operating line: provisioning took profit before tax down to 1,873.72m, and the tax charge then consumed 76.9% of what remained (1,441.08m of 1,873.72m). Southeast Bank's effective tax rate is chronically high — it ranged from 31.9% to 55.9% in eleven of the fifteen years — but FY2024's 76.9% is the series peak and FY2017's 72.1% the second, and those are precisely the two years with the heaviest provisioning, consistent with loan-loss provisions being disallowed for tax purposes and taxed profit diverging sharply from accounting profit.

Balance-sheet expansion has essentially stopped. Total assets grew at a 12.75% compound annual rate over FY2011-FY2020 (158,078.59m to 465,293.41m) but only 3.57% a year over FY2020-FY2025 (to 554,424.56m). FY2022 is the only year in the 15-year series in which the balance sheet shrank: total assets fell 0.55% and deposits fell 1.48% (376,700.77m to 371,143.44m). Gross loans grew just 12.17% cumulatively across the four years FY2021-FY2025 (336,329.37m to 377,258.69m), and only 1.17% in FY2025 itself while deposits grew 6.78% — the bank is taking in funds it is not lending out.

The cost-to-income ratio has nearly doubled over the series, from 25.50% (FY2011) to a peak of 47.21% (FY2023), settling at 39.56% in FY2025. Headcount rose from 1,848 to 3,226 and branches from 84 to 137 over the same period, but net profit per branch (net profit after tax divided by year-end branch count) was 22.76m in FY2011, 3.20m in FY2024 and 24.45m in FY2025 — meaning the branch network delivered essentially no earnings growth across fifteen years of expansion, and none at all in nominal-per-branch terms.

The market has de-rated the shares continuously. Price-to-book fell from 1.34x (FY2011, price 31.10 vs NAV 23.29) to 0.35x (FY2025, price 9.00 vs NAV 25.74), and has been below 1.0x in every year since FY2012. Net asset value per share is essentially flat across fifteen years (23.29 to 25.74, +10.5%) while the share price fell 71.1% — the equity has compounded almost nothing for shareholders over the full period.

FY2020's apparent asset-quality strength is a regulatory artefact, not performance: the reported NPL ratio fell to a series-low 3.10% and specific provision coverage spiked to 203.49% because Bangladesh Bank's COVID-era moratorium suspended loan downgrades for the year. The underlying deterioration surfaced immediately once the moratorium lapsed — classified loans rose 61.33% in FY2021 and kept rising for three more years. Any trend line drawn through FY2020 will understate the deterioration that began before it.

The credit-deposit ratio has run at 83-86% for most of the last decade — 85.81% (FY2023), 85.49% (FY2024), 83.32% (FY2025) — versus 76.44% at its FY2013 low. This leaves comparatively little unlent deposit headroom, though the FY2025 easing to 83.32% (deposits +6.78% against loans +1.17%) is a modest improvement in the funding buffer.

Newly available Q1-Q3 interim data (from the bank's own embedded 'Evaluation of the Quarterly Financials' disclosure table, FY2016-FY2025) shows that in 7 of the 9 years where a discrete Q4 can be isolated, cumulative net profit after tax at year-end was LOWER than at the 30-September (9-month) mark -- i.e. Southeast Bank posted a discrete fourth-quarter LOSS: FY2017 (9-month 2,367m -> full-year 1,169m, Q4 alone -1,198m), FY2019 (3,276m -> 2,509m, -767m), FY2020 (2,769m -> 2,149m, -620m), FY2021 (3,717m -> 1,784m, -1,933m), FY2022 (3,439m -> 1,752m, -1,687m), FY2023 (3,005m -> 2,134m, -871m) and FY2024 (1,570m -> 433m, -1,137m, the most severe). In every year from FY2020-FY2024 where the provisioning line is separately broken out in this table, the cause is directly visible: cumulative 'Provision for loans and advances/investments and others' jumps sharply in the Q4-only increment versus the first nine months -- FY2020 +3,823m (vs 1,286m in 9 months), FY2021 +4,034m (vs 1,379m), FY2022 +3,688m (vs 2,905m), FY2023 +3,503m (vs 1,841m), FY2024 +4,217m (vs 5,631m, the largest Q4-alone charge in the series). Operating performance before provisioning is NOT the driver -- cumulative 'Profit before provision' increases monotonically every single quarter in every year with no exception -- so this is specifically a year-end provisioning-timing pattern, not weaker underlying operations in Q4. Only FY2016 (Q4 +155m), FY2018 (Q4 +1m, effectively flat) and FY2025 (Q4 +1,393m, still with a further 2,212m Q4 provisioning increment but not enough to erase the quarter's operating profit) broke the pattern. This means any analysis using only Q1-Q3 (or annualizing a 9-month run-rate) would have materially OVERSTATED full-year profitability in most years of this series, and the timing itself -- provisioning decisions concentrated at year-end rather than recognised progressively as asset quality data becomes available intra-year -- is itself a data point on provisioning discipline, independent of the FY2024 and FY2025 asset-quality findings already in this file.

insights.historical_context: Southeast Bank's fifteen-year record divides cleanly into three phases. Through FY2011-FY2014 it was a high-return mid-sized private commercial bank: ROE 10.5-16.5%, NPL 3.5-4.5%, cost-to-income in the mid-20s, and a balance sheet compounding at roughly 13% a year. From FY2015 the returns broke down — ROE fell below 12% and never recovered to the earlier level, hitting 4.46% as early as FY2017 alongside the first regulatory capital shortfall — while the balance sheet kept growing, so the bank was getting steadily larger and steadily less profitable at the same time. The third phase, FY2021 onward, is an asset-quality crisis: four straight years of 40-62% annual growth in classified loans took NPLs from 3.10% to 14.82% by FY2024 and all but eliminated earnings (net profit 432.64m, ROE 1.36%), with a second capital shortfall in that year. FY2025 reports a sharp reversal — NPL halved to 7.51%, ROE back to 10.16%, capital surplus restored — but the composition of that reversal is the central question for anyone using this data: specific provision coverage fell to 39.36% and total loan-loss provisions were released by 10,036.35m, an amount of the same order as the entire improvement in pre-tax profit. The structural backdrop is worse than the headline ratios suggest: net interest margin has compressed by three quarters since FY2016 to 0.43%, leaving the bank dependent on non-interest income, and the market has priced this accordingly at 0.35x book.

sources.note: This is a BSEC-mandated corporate-governance disclosure ('Evaluation of the Quarterly Financials by the Audit Committee and by the Board' -- title wording varies slightly year to year, e.g. 'by the Audit Committee & by the Board'). Most banks answer this disclosure requirement with a checkbox; Southeast Bank answers it with an actual data table giving Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4 balance-sheet and income-statement figures for that report's own year plus a comparative column for the prior year. Balance-sheet items are period-end snapshots (basis reported); income-statement items and EPS are CUMULATIVE FROM 1 JANUARY of that year, exactly as the table's own column headers state (e.g. '1 Jan'21 to 30 Sep'21') -- stored with the _cumulative normalised-name suffix, matching CITYBANK's convention. The table's structure changed twice across the 2016-2025 span: (1) 2016-2019 report a single combined 'Loans and advances/investments' line (stored as loans_advances_and_investments_combined) with no Non-Controlling-Interest row and no split of loan-loss provisions from tax provisions; (2) 2021-2022 split Investments from Loans and Advances, added an explicit Non-Controlling Interest row (~10m), added a separate 'Total non-interest income' row, and split 'Provision for loans and advances/investments and others' from 'Provision for taxation'; (3) 2023-2025 additionally add a 'Perpetual bond' line. Genuinely confirmed ABSENT for FY2011-FY2015: a full-text search of every annual report FY2011-FY2025 for this table's heading (in every capitalisation/wording variant observed) and for its distinctive '1st/2nd/3rd/4th Qtr.' column-header pattern found zero matches in FY2011-FY2015; the FY2014 report's own 'Report of the Audit Committee' section (pp.79-81), read in full as a direct check, is pure narrative describing Audit Committee meetings and duties with no data table. FY2020's own report contains this table's heading, column structure and closing regulatory paragraph but every numeric data row failed to extract (empty/garbled) -- the same underlying subsetted-embedded-font issue already documented elsewhere in this file for FY2020's other summary table -- so FY2020 is sourced entirely from the FY2021 report's comparative column instead (see the dedicated FY2020 entry below). VALIDATION: balance-sheet identity (Total assets = Total liabilities + Total equity [+ Non-controlling interest from 2021 on]) holds in every quarter of every year to within rounding for the 2021-2025 vintage, and to within a small, consistent ~BDT 8-11m gap (~0.002-0.004% of total assets) for the 2015-2020 vintage -- most plausibly a small Non-Controlling-Interest balance not yet broken out as its own row in the earlier vintage (the 2021+ vintage's explicit NCI row is almost exactly this size). Cumulative net profit after tax was checked for monotonic Q1->Q2->Q3 increase in every year: it holds without exception. NOTABLE CROSS-YEAR FINDING (see insights.json): cumulative net profit after tax was LOWER at year-end (Q4) than at the 30-September (Q3) mark in 7 of the 11 years now covered by this table (2017, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024) -- i.e. Southeast Bank posted a discrete fourth-quarter LOSS in those years -- driven by a large loan-loss-provisioning catch-up concentrated in Q4 (directly visible in the 'Provision for loans and advances/investments and others' cumulative line for 2020-2024, where it's broken out separately). This pattern is not visible from annual-only data and is a genuinely new finding from this Q1-Q3 backfill pass.

sources.source_document: southeastb-q1-2026.pdf ('Consolidated Balance Sheet/Off-balance Sheet Items/Profit and Loss Account/Cash Flow Statement As at/For the period ended 31 March 2026, Provisional and unaudited', 14 pages); southeastb-h1-2026-cookie.pdf ('...For the halfyear ended 30 June 2026, Provisional and unaudited', 17 pages) -- the bank's own separately-filed quarterly PDFs, NOT the annual-report-embedded 'Evaluation of the Quarterly Financials' table used for FY2015-2025 (no FY2026 annual report exists yet to carry that table)
sources.note: ACCESS: the documented F5/BIG-IP WAF (fake HTTP 200 with a ~46KB 'Request Rejected' HTML body) was re-confirmed for plain curl against BOTH quarters' PDF URLs this session. Two different successful workarounds were needed: (1) for the 6.9MB Q1 file, the WebFetch tool retrieved the genuine PDF directly, where curl could not -- WebFetch appears to use a fetch path the WAF's bot-detection doesn't block. (2) for the 12.45MB H1 file, WebFetch itself failed (exceeds its 10MB response cap -- confirmed via a `curl -I` HEAD request, which itself succeeded and returned genuine PDF headers: Content-Length 12,451,950, Content-Type application/pdf, plus F5 session/affinity cookies); re-issuing a GET with those captured cookies via curl then succeeded, meaning the WAF's block on this specific endpoint was session/cookie-state-dependent rather than an absolute block. EXTRACTION: both PDFs contain genuine embedded text (pdftotext -layout, NOT a blank scan -- unlike SHAHJABANK's 2026 filings), but a subsetted font renders several digit glyphs incorrectly in a consistent, decodable pattern ('t'/'I'/'l' for '1', 's' for '5', and in the Q1 filing specifically a '4'-for-'1' substitution in a few large totals). Every figure was decoded and independently validated against at least one arithmetic identity (component sums, balance-sheet identity, A=NII+non-interest income, C=A-B, PBT=C-D, PAT=PBT-Tax) before being used. GENUINE ERROR FOUND (not a decode artifact): the Q1 filing's own printed 'Total liabilities' (519,834,209,074) is arithmetically WRONG by exactly 30,000,000,000 against its own listed components (which sum to 549,834,209,074) and against Total Assets minus Equity minus NCI (also 549,834,209,074, exact) -- the corrected figure is used, per the arithmetically-impossible-figure project convention; the H1 filing has no equivalent error. STRONG CROSS-VALIDATION: the two independently-downloaded filings agree to the taka -- Q1's own printed PAT (1,317,869,696) exactly equals H1's cumulative PAT (2,187,698,866) minus H1's own bonus discrete-Q2 PAT column (869,829,170). Both quarters' EPS (0.99 and, cumulative, 1.64) also match DSE's own live 'Interim Financial Performance: 2026' table (dsebd.org/displayCompany.php?name=SOUTHEASTB) exactly, a third independent source, itself confirming NOT-WAF-blocked access to dsebd.org for this bank's live interim EPS/price data. BASIS: both filings are CONSOLIDATED (matching this bank's established basis throughout its 15-year annual series), but each ALSO discloses a bonus Solo-basis comparison in its own Notes 5/6 (Q1: Solo PAT 1,247.03m/EPS 0.93 vs Consolidated 1,317.87m/EPS 0.99, Solo NAV/share 26.40 vs Consolidated 26.49; H1: Solo PAT 1,997.19m/EPS 1.49 vs Consolidated 2,187.70m/EPS 1.64, Solo NAV/share 26.98 vs Consolidated 27.16) -- confirming the real, small, consistent Consolidated-vs-Solo gap already documented for this bank, now visible at interim granularity for the first time. NOTABLE FINDING: Net Interest Income turned negative for the first time in this dataset's SOUTHEASTB series (-718m cumulative at Q1, deepening to -1,631m at H1) -- interest expense now exceeds interest income -- yet the bank remains solidly profitable and growing (PAT 1,318m at Q1, 2,188m cumulative at H1) purely on non-interest income growth (Investment income, Commission/Exchange/Brokerage), a materially different shape from the interest-margin-driven crises documented elsewhere in this dataset (PREMIERBAN, ABBANK, etc.) -- worth flagging as a genuinely new development, not visible in FY2025's annual data (positive NII throughout that year). Full detail in bank_financials/SOUTHEASTB/quarterly/2026_Q1.json, 2026_Q2.json.

UPDATE 2026-09-12: direct retrieval of the bank's own separately-filed unaudited interim statements WAS attempted and succeeded for 2026 Q1/H1 -- see the dedicated '2026 Q1/Q2' source entry above for the full WAF-bypass method (WebFetch for the smaller file, a cookie-session curl workaround for the larger one) and validation detail. DSE's own live interim table (dsebd.org/displayCompany.php?name=SOUTHEASTB) was also confirmed as a genuine, unblocked, independent cross-check source for EPS/price data going forward. UPDATE 2026-08-26 (superseded for 2026 by the above): direct retrieval of the bank's own separately-filed unaudited interim (Q1/H1/Q3) financial statements was NOT attempted in this pass -- southeastbank.com.bd's WAF block (documented elsewhere in this file) would still apply, and DSE's news archive remains the untried fallback for that route. Instead, a superior alternative was found and used: Southeast Bank's own ANNUAL reports for FY2016-FY2025 each embed a BSEC-mandated 'Evaluation of the Quarterly Financials by the Audit Committee and by the Board' disclosure table giving actual Q1/Q2/Q3(/Q4) balance-sheet and cumulative-income-statement figures for that year plus a comparative column for the prior year -- see the dedicated 'annual_report_embedded_quarterly_table' entries above/below for the full sourcing, cross-check and restatement detail. This resolves Q1-Q3 for FY2015-FY2025 (11 years; FY2015 and FY2020 single-sourced from an adjacent year's comparative column, the other 9 years contemporaneously sourced and cross-checked). Confirmed genuinely UNAVAILABLE by this route: FY2011-FY2014 (the table itself does not exist in any report that far back -- verified by full-text search of every report and a direct read of the FY2014 Audit Committee section) and FY2026 (no annual report exists yet for a year still in progress). Those years remain open only to the original DSE-news-archive route, not yet attempted.
